Focus on a full inferential workflow by stimulation paradigm using only:

- Average Speed
- AD

- ICMS Only
- Dim Visual Only
- Bright Visual Only

- post-hoc analysis
- a multiple-comparison correction strategy
- a predictive model for stimulation paradigm based on the performance variables

{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct five separate one-way ANOVAs with Stim Paradigm as the between-subjects factor for each continuous response: Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD",
    "For Success (binary), use one-way logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than classical ANOVA",
    "Given the large sample size (n=76655), check for violations of normality and homoscedasticity; if severe, apply Welch's ANOVA or bootstrap-based inference",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect or blocking factor in mixed-effects models to account for repeated measures structure (8 mice, unequal observations per mouse)"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous outcomes with significant omnibus tests, perform Tukey's HSD pairwise comparisons across the 5 stimulation paradigms",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise z-tests for proportions with adjusted confidence intervals",
    "Report effect sizes (Cohen's d for continuous, odds ratios for Success) alongside p-values",
    "Focus comparisons on Combined vs. single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and all active conditions vs. Sham"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across all tests: apply separately within each outcome variable (10 pairwise comparisons per continuous outcome, 10 for Success), with overall family-wise error controlled at alpha=0.05",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression (or softmax regression) with Stim Paradigm as the categorical response and Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD as predictors. This is appropriate because: (1) the response is strictly categorical with 5 unordered levels, (2) ordinary linear regression would inappropriately impose ordinality and equal spacing assumptions, and (3) the multinomial model directly estimates the probability of each stimulation paradigm given performance profiles. Random forest or gradient boosting classifiers should also be considered as ensemble alternatives for robustness checking, with cross-validation to assess predictive accuracy.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals of each ANOVA; given n=76655, central limit theorem provides robustness but check for extreme skewness (note Path Efficiency max=29.8 suggests right skew)",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equality of variances; consider Welch's ANOVA if violated",
    "Independence: Account for clustering by Mouse using mixed-effects models or cluster-robust standard errors",
    "Multicollinearity: Check variance inflation factors (VIF) among predictors in multinomial model; AD and Path Efficiency may covary",
    "Complete separation in multinomial model: Check for empty cells in predictor space by outcome category"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows superior performance (faster Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency) compared to single-modality conditions based on typical multisensory integration effects",
    "ICMS Only may outperform visual-only conditions given the task's dependence on whisker-based navigation",
    "Sham expected to show lowest performance across metrics serving as baseline",
    "Bright Visual Only may outperform Dim Visual Only due to better visibility",
    "AD (angular dispersion) expected to be lowest for Combined and highest for Sham, reflecting more direct trajectories with effective stimulation",
    "Predictive model accuracy likely moderate-to-high given substantial mean differences between paradigms (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505)"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance in Stim Paradigm: Combined (63.7%), ICMS Only (14.8%), Dim Visual Only (12.5%), Sham (4.6%), Bright Visual Only (4.3%) — this complicates predictive modeling and reduces power for Sham and Bright Visual comparisons",
    "No trial-level temporal information or learning effects captured in current data view",
    "Mouse identity confounded with stimulation condition assignment; need mixed-effects approach",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme right skew (max=29.8, mean=0.47, sd=0.47) suggesting bimodal or mixture distribution",
    "Success is binary but analyzed alongside continuous measures; different statistical frameworks required",
    "Single replication (run 169, replication 2) — results may not generalize across experimental batches",
    "Temperature=0.75 and model-specific prompting may introduce LLM-specific variability not captured here"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Execute the multinomial logistic regression with mouse-level random effects as the primary predictive model, with sensitivity analyses using: (1) multinomial probit for robustness, (2) ordinal logistic regression if a clear performance-based ordering of paradigms emerges, and (3) machine learning classifiers (random forest, XGBoost) with stratified cross-validation to handle class imbalance. Report classification accuracy, macro-averaged F1, and per-class precision/recall given the severe imbalance favoring Combined stimulation."
}
